summary: Unexpected negative line on March invoice after reserved capacity failover and late credit application
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightChat reported a negative invoice line item on the March 1-10 provisional invoice. The negative line is labeled 'reserve-credit-adjustment' and appears after a Dedicated -> Hosted fallback event on 2026-03-07 02:17 UTC. Customer expects reserved hourly credits to have applied during the fallback window; instead we see a late, negative adjustment that increased the net charge for the mid-cycle period.

Impact:
- Customer sees a $2,318 negative adjustment (reduces credit) on provisional invoice; customer concerned they'll be overcharged when invoice finalizes.
- Affects production traffic for BrightChat; they had autoscaling fallbacks to Hosted for approx 3h on 2026-03-07.

Environment:
- Account: brightchat-prod (org id: oc-98f7b3)
- Tier: Dedicated with reserved hours (mixed-hosted fallback enabled)
- Region: us-east-1
- Timezone/DST: Customer operates in America/New_York (DST change occurred last week)

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior:
1) Confirm dedicated pool saturation and automatic fallback event recorded at 2026-03-07T02:17:12Z (scheduler logs).
2) Validate daily/hourly accumulator shows reserved-hour credit not applied for 02:00-05:00 window on 2026-03-07; postback reconciler later inserted a negative adjustment on 2026-03-08 03:05:42Z labeled reserve-credit-reconciliation.
3) Provisional invoice generated 2026-03-10 shows negative reserve-credit-adjustment line (-$2,318).

Expected behavior:
- Reserved hourly credits should have been prorated and applied to hosted-fallback usage at the reserved rate or neutralized via fallback billing policy. Any adjustments should be idempotent and appear as positive credits for the customer, not negative offsets that increase the charge.

Attachments/Logs:
- scheduler/fallback-events lines 2026-03-07 02:17 UTC (attached)
- hourly-accumulator dump for brightchat-prod 2026-03-07 (attached)
- billing postback logs 2026-03-08 (attached)
- provisional invoice (PDF) 2026-03-10 (attached)
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Maria (BrightChat Support Lead): We noticed the provisional invoice had a -$2,318 line called reserve-credit-adjustment. We did not change our reserved capacity during the billing window. Please advise; this looks like we owe Redwood money rather than the other way around.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Elena Park (Support): Acknowledged. Opening ticket and escalating to Billing team. Requesting relevant logs and provisional invoice attachments. SLA P1 noted. Marcus Chen will take point on engineering investigation.

2026-03-10 13:22 - Marcus Chen (Billing Engineer): Initial triage: I can see the fallback event and a postback from the hourly reconciler that ran after the fallback. Hypothesis: postback ordering + DST shift caused the reserved-hour tag to be removed then re-applied with opposite sign. Pulling raw postback events and accumulator snapshots now.

2026-03-11 09:40 - SRE (Anita Ruiz): Scheduler logs confirm fallback window 02:17-05:23 UTC. We observed clock drift warnings between aggregator nodes in us-east at 02:20 UTC; nodes were behind by ~2 minutes. I'm attaching aggregator node health and ntp sync events. No evidence of double-billing at the serving layer (no duplicate req ids).

2026-03-11 15:08 - Billing (Marcus Chen): Found two reconciler runs: one at 2026-03-07T05:05:10Z (initial, applied +reserved-credit tags) and a later compensating run at 2026-03-08T03:05:42Z that issued a negative adjustment. The compensating run was triggered by a late postback from an ingestion worker that had an older timestamp due to DST-related ingestion windowing. I'm preparing a draft fix to be prioritized (PR referenced).

2026-03-12 08:30 - Elena Park (Support): Shared interim workaround with customer: we can issue a manual credit to offset the negative line while engineering resolves root cause. Customer requested manual credit and confirmation before final invoice generation.
2026-03-12 12:05 - Maria (BrightChat): Thank you. Please proceed with manual credit and keep us posted on the code fix timeline. We need this cleared before 2026-03-15.

2026-03-12 14:18 - Marcus Chen (Billing): Manual credit of $2,318 applied to provisional account balance (internal adjustment id: ADJ-88122). This will reflect in the preview immediately; follow-up: schedule a hotfix to prevent out-of-order reconciler compensations across DST and regional ingestion windows.
investigation_notes: Timestamps: Several ingestion workers in us-east were using local time windows that did not account for recent DST change; late postbacks were ingested with timestamps placing them before reconciler window leading to compensating runs.

Accumulator behavior: hourly-accumulator uses a sliding-window key by hour-start in UTC. When late postbacks arrive with epoch timestamps that map to prior hour boundaries, reconciler may issue corrections; race conditions with initial postback created a negative adjustment later.

Edge-case observed: dedicated->hosted fallback currently tags usage as 'fallback:hosted' and expects reserved-credit reconcile to neutralize cost. Reconcile logic erroneously inverts sign if reconciler run identifies duplicate tag sets and a late postback removes an earlier credit entry rather than consolidating.

Related code: billing/reconciler/service (PR 2491) contains logic for idempotency key generation. Current generation uses hour_start + org_id + node_id; node_id variance caused duplicate keys in this incident.
SRE note: aggregator node ntp drift amplified the effect; we should add stricter ntp alerts during DST windows and ensure ingestion workers use monotonic event time where possible.
resolution_notes: Workaround: Manual credit ADJ-88122 issued to BrightChat for $2,318 on 2026-03-12 14:18. Customer confirmed receipt in portal. (Pending final invoice reconciliation.)

Short-term fix: Rollback of reconciler idempotency change that allowed node_id to affect key generation. Rollback scheduled to staging 2026-03-13; hotfix to production pending post-staging validation.

Long-term mitigation: Update reconciler to compute idempotency key using deterministic hour_start + org_id + reserved_pool_id and ignore node_id; add explicit handling for late postbacks arriving outside a 24-hour grace window. Add unit + integration tests for DST edge cases.
Follow-ups assigned: BILL-52 (implement key-change and tests), SRE-78 (improve ntp monitoring), OPS-134 (backfill re-run for accounts affected by late-postbacks between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-14).
